question: Procedural urgency in Case No. 14.724 (deadline 16 August 2026)

In Case No. 14.724, concerning the 1981 enforced disappearance of two civilians by Salvadoran State forces, the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights (IACHR) granted El Salvador a final extension, expiring on 16 August 2026, to comply with Merits Report No. 262/23.

Should El Salvador remain non-compliant, the case may be referred to the InterAmerican Court of Human Rights, as the petitioners have formally requested, having also submitted a full reparation proposal. El Salvador has used successive extensions to delay rather than cooperate in good faith, a pattern relevant to the EU’s broader engagement on human rights and the rule of law in Central America. 1.
Is the European External Action Service following the imminent 16 August 2026 deadline in Case No. 14.724?
Will the EU convey to the Salvadoran authorities the importance of complying in good faith with the IACHR’s recommendations before that date?
Will the EU support the referral of Case No. 14.724 to the IACHR by diplomatic means should El Salvador fail to comply?
answer: The European External Action Service closely follows the human rights and rule of law situation in El Salvador, including issues of transitional justice and accountability for serious human rights violations committed during the armed conflict.

The EU regularly recalls, in its contacts with the Salvadoran authorities, the importance of cooperating fully with international and regional human rights mechanisms and of giving appropriate follow-up to their recommendations. The EU will continue to raise human rights, the rule of law and accountability in its dialogue with El Salvador.

The EU does not comment publicly on confidential exchanges concerning individual cases. The decision whether to refer a case to the Inter-American Court of Human Rights falls within the independent mandate of the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights, in accordance with the American Convention on Human Rights and the InterAmerican Commission’s Rules of Procedure (1).
The EU fully respects the independence of the Inter-American human rights system and supports effective cooperation by States with its institutions.
